brief.paper_summary:
由于现实世界中的大多数数据都可以用图表示，因此近年来针对图表示学
习的研究越来越受到关注。通过将高维图数据转化成低维的表征向量，图表示
学习可以有效地对图的信息进行存储并快捷地访问图中实体的关键知识。利用
学习到的图表征数据可以为社交网络行为分析、节点分类、链路预测和聚类等
下游任务提供帮助。随着深度学习的快速发展，研究人员提出了基于图神经网
络的图表示学习方法，其使图中的节点能够同时学习图的结构信息以及邻域节
点的特征信息，从而得到高质量的低维表征。针对图神经网络上的图表示学
习，本文主要关注两个问题：大规模时序图场景下的图表示学习方法和分布式
场景下的大规模图的图神经网络优化训练方法。
真实世界中的图数据规模往往十分庞大且处于动态变化的状态，而现有的
图神经网络要么无法处理动态时序图上的图表征学习，要么面对大规模图数据
集时训练效率低下。为了解决大规模动态图上的图表征学习问题，本文提出了
一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法——GSAERU 模型。GSAERU 模
型由“图表征学习模块”和“时序学习模块”两部分构成。首先将动态时序图
建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列，接着在单时间步上将图快照输入图表征学习
模块。该模块通过图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，并将压缩后的新图输入图自编
码器，利用和原图的重构误差训练原图节点的表征。在获得单时间步上的图表
征后将其输入时序学习模块，并通过一个循环神经网络学习原图在时间维度上
的特征信息与依赖关系，从而得到大规模时序图的高质量表征。基于在四个真
实世界的大规模图数据集上的大量实验表明，GSAERU 模型能够高效生成时序
图的表征。与传统的图神经网络算法相比，其平均内存消耗和平均训练时长只
有其9.86% 与13.27%，且与性能最好的算法在大部分指标下的差距都不超过
3.5%。

ii
使用分布式技术加速神经网络训练也是如今热门的研究课题，因为在处理
大规模数据时，单个设备（如CPU，GPU）有限的内存和计算资源往往会成为
训练瓶颈。而分布式技术可以提供更多的计算资源来提高训练效率。然而由于
图数据的不规则性，传统分布式机器学习方法中的子任务划分和模型训练方法
难以直接应用于图神经网络。针对大规模图流数据场景下的分布式图神经网络
训练优化问题，本文提出了基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络优化训练算法——
DSGNN 模型。DSGNN 模型采用“领导——工作者”工作模式，首先由领导节
点利用一个基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分并将划分子图分配给各
个工作节点。工作节点随后执行一个基于图摘要技术的小批量训练并将训练结
果通过一个注意力层返回给领导节点，最后由领导节点汇总结果并计算梯度，
并根据梯度同步更新所有计算节点上的模型。基于四个真实世界的大规模图数
据集上的大量实验，结果表明DSGNN 模型可以大大加速GNN 模型的训练，
并且在链路预测任务上的F1 分数显著高于其它分布式图神经网络模型。
brief.research_problem: 面向大规模动态图的图神经网络优化机制研究

novelty_points.claim: 提出了一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法GSAERU，该方法结合图摘要技术和图自编码器，并利用循环神经网络学习时间维度的特征与依赖关系，能够高效生成大规模动态时序图的表征，显著降低内存消耗和训练时间。
novelty_points.claim_en: Proposed a large-scale sequential graph representation learning method GSAERU based on graph summarization, which combines graph summarization with graph autoencoder and uses recurrent neural networks to learn temporal features and dependencies, enabling efficient representation generation for large-scale dynamic graphs with significantly reduced memory consumption and training time.
technical_features: 将动态时序图建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列
利用图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，将压缩后的新图输入图自编码器，通过重构误差训练原图节点的表征
引入循环神经网络作为时序学习模块，学习原图在时间维度上的特征信息与依赖关系
在四个真实世界大规模图数据集上验证，平均内存消耗和平均训练时长分别仅为传统图神经网络算法的9.86%和13.27%
technical_features_en: Modeling dynamic sequential graphs as a sequence of snapshots of the original graph at each moment
Compressing the original graph via graph summarization and feeding the compressed graph into a graph autoencoder, using reconstruction error to train node representations of the original graph
Introducing a recurrent neural network as the time sequence learning module to learn feature information and dependencies of the original graph in the temporal dimension

Extensive experiments on four real-world large-scale graph datasets demonstrate that average memory consumption and average training time are only 9.86% and 13.27% of those of traditional graph neural network algorithms

novelty_points.claim: 提出了一种基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络优化训练算法DSGNN，采用“领导—工作者”工作模式，通过基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分，工作节点执行基于图摘要的小批量训练，并通过注意力层将结果汇总至领导节点，实现大规模图流数据上GNN训练的高效加速。
novelty_points.claim_en: Proposed a distributed graph neural network optimization training algorithm DSGNN based on graph summarization, which adopts a leader-worker mode, partitions the original graph using a graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation, workers perform mini-batch training based on graph summarization, and results are summarized to the leader through an attention layer, enabling efficient acceleration of GNN training on large-scale graph streaming data.
technical_features: 采用“领导—工作者”工作模式，由领导节点划分图并分配子图，工作者节点负责训练
基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分，适应图数据的不规则性
工作节点执行基于图摘要的小批量训练，压缩子图以降低计算量
训练结果通过注意力层返回给领导节点，领导节点汇总并计算梯度，同步更新所有计算节点模型
technical_features_en: Adopting a leader-worker mode where the leader partitions the graph and assigns subgraphs to workers, and workers are responsible for training
A graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation partitions the original graph, accommodating the irregularity of graph data
Workers perform mini-batch training based on graph summarization, compressing subgraphs to reduce computation
Training results are returned to the leader through an attention layer, and the leader aggregates results and computes gradients, synchronously updating models on all computing nodes

novelty_points.claim: 在分布式图神经网络训练中，提出了基于边分割的图流划分算法，用于将大规模图数据划分为多个子图并分配给工作者节点，有效解决了图数据不规则性导致的分布式训练难点，提升了训练效率。
novelty_points.claim_en: In distributed graph neural network training, a graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation is proposed to partition large-scale graph data into multiple subgraphs and assign them to worker nodes, effectively addressing the difficulties caused by irregularity of graph data in distributed training and improving training efficiency.
technical_features: 基于边分割的图流划分算法将原图划分为子图，适用于图流数据场景
划分后的子图分配给各工作节点，实现并行处理
该算法能够适应动态图流数据的变化，提高分布式训练的扩展性
technical_features_en: A graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation partitions the original graph into subgraphs, suitable for graph streaming data scenarios
The partitioned subgraphs are assigned to worker nodes for parallel processing
The algorithm adapts to changes in dynamic graph streaming data, improving scalability of distributed training

evidence_cards.document_title: Efficient Learning-based Graph Simulation for Temporal Graphs
evidence_cards.main_contribution: TGAE proposes an efficient learning-based approach using a temporal graph autoencoder to generate graph snapshots for temporal graphs, achieving good simulation quality and efficiency.
overlaps: Both use graph autoencoders for temporal/dynamic graphs
Both handle temporal graphs composed of evolving graph snapshots
differences: TGAE is designed for graph generation/simulation, whereas GSAERU is for node representation learning on large-scale dynamic graphs
TGAE does not use graph summarization to compress the original graph; GSAERU compresses the graph via summarization before autoencoder training
TGAE does not use a recurrent neural network for temporal feature learning; GSAERU introduces an RNN as a temporal learning module
TGAE focuses on simulation quality and efficiency of graph generation, not on reducing memory consumption and training time for representation learning

sources.title: Efficient Learning-based Graph Simulation for Temporal Graphs
sources.quote: we propose an efficient learning-based approach to generate graph snapshots, namely temporal graph autoencoder (TGAE)

evidence_cards.document_title: Scalable and Efficient Joint Spiking Embedding Predictive Architecture for Large-Scale Dynamic Graphs
evidence_cards.main_contribution: SG-JEPA proposes a joint spiking embedding predictive architecture for large-scale dynamic graph representation learning, achieving superior training efficiency and memory scalability compared with prior self-supervised dynamic graph baselines.
overlaps: Both address large-scale dynamic graph representation learning with efficiency gains in training time and memory
Both handle sequential/temporal inputs from dynamic graphs
Both aim to generate task-agnostic graph embeddings for large-scale dynamic graphs
differences: SG-JEPA uses spiking neural networks and a joint embedding predictive architecture, whereas GSAERU combines graph summarization with a graph autoencoder
SG-JEPA does not compress the original graph via graph summarization; GSAERU explicitly compresses the graph before feeding it into the autoencoder
SG-JEPA does not use reconstruction error to train node representations; GSAERU trains node representations via reconstruction error on the compressed graph
SG-JEPA does not use a recurrent neural network as a dedicated temporal learning module; GSAERU introduces an RNN to learn temporal features and dependencies

sources.title: Scalable and Efficient Joint Spiking Embedding Predictive Architecture for Large-Scale Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: we propose SG-JEPA, a joint spiking embedding predictive architecture for large-scale dynamic graphs

sources.title: Scalable and Efficient Joint Spiking Embedding Predictive Architecture for Large-Scale Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: SG-JEPA avoids the complex machinery (negative sampling, graph augmentations, edge-level reconstruction, etc.), resulting in superior training efficiency and memory scalability compared with prior self-supervised dynamic graph baselines.

evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
evidence_cards.main_contribution: Designs AGL, a scalable, fault-tolerant, and integrated system for GNN training and inference using MapReduce-based message passing.
overlaps: Distributed GNN training on large-scale graphs
differences: Does not use graph summarization for training
Does not adopt a leader-worker mode
Does not use edge-based graph flow partitioning
Does not use attention layer for result aggregation

sources.title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
sources.quote: In this paper, we design AGL, a scalable, fault-tolerance and integrated system, with fully-functional training and inference for GNNs.

evidence_cards.main_contribution: Presents AliGraph, a comprehensive graph neural network system with distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators, and runtime to support GNN training at scale.
overlaps: Distributed GNN training on large-scale graphs
differences: Does not use graph summarization for training
Does not adopt a leader-worker mode
Does not use edge-based graph flow partitioning
Does not use attention layer for result aggregation

differences: Not distributed
Does not use graph summarization

differences: Not distributed
Does not use graph summarization
Does not adopt a leader-worker mode

sources.title: GraphSAINT: Graph Sampling Based Inductive Learning Method
sources.quote: We propose GraphSAINT, a graph sampling based inductive learning method that improves training efficiency and accuracy in a fundamentally different way.

evidence_cards.document_title: HGP-IC: graph neural networks via hotness-based partitioning and information compensation
evidence_cards.main_contribution: HGP-IC proposes a refined graph partitioning strategy (HGP) combined with information compensation (IC) for GNN training on large-scale graphs, addressing the challenges of edge partitioning where nodes cannot access all their original neighbors during subgraph training.
overlaps: Both address edge-based graph partitioning for GNN training on large-scale graphs
Both aim to split large graphs into subgraphs to enable training on limited resources
Both address the irregularity and memory constraints of large-scale graph data in distributed/local training
differences: HGP-IC focuses on static graph partitioning with information compensation for local learning, not on a graph flow (streaming) partition algorithm
HGP-IC does not explicitly address dynamic graph streaming data changes or adapting partitions to evolving graphs

HGP-IC's approach combines partitioning with information compensation (IC) to restore lost neighbor information, whereas the novelty point describes a flow-based partition algorithm for assigning subgraphs to worker nodes

sources.title: HGP-IC: graph neural networks via hotness-based partitioning and information compensation
sources.quote: Existing graph partitioning methods fall into node and edge partitioning. Node partitioning drops inter-subgraph edges, causing incomplete information, while edge partitioning, though structure-preserving, introduces two major challenges

sources.title: HGP-IC: graph neural networks via hotness-based partitioning and information compensation
sources.quote: the "graph partitioning $$ + $$ + local learning" framework splits the global graph into smaller subgraphs for independent training
